opening.argument: The video explains a standard affiliate-marketing process rather than presenting a deceptive offer. It defines the arrangement as promoting a service or product and receiving a commission when a referred person purchases it, then explains that participants apply to a program, receive unique account-linked links, and place them in videos, blog posts, or social-media content. The discussion also limits its earning claims: affiliate marketing is expressly described as not a get-rich-quick scheme and as requiring time to build income, with payouts potentially taking 30 to 90 days. The advice is framed around using links when relevant to the content. Nothing described requires payment or personal-data submission, identifies a victim loss, promises a misleading outcome, or offers a specific deceptive transaction.

citations.quote: affiliate marketing is basically advertising someones service or product and when a person purchases that service or product you earn a commission from that referral.
first, you apply to the program. Number two, once you got accepted into the program, then you'll be provided links. These links are unique to you. And they trace back to your account.
